To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

serum levels of CRP and IL6 on day 1 of treatment are independently associated with a high risk of treatment failure in community acquired pneumonia, and low levels of PCT on day one of treatment have a high negative predictive power for early treatment failure.
serum levels of CRP and IL6 on days 1 or 3 and of PCT on days one and three were independently associated with treatment failure in patients with CAP.

Serum levels of cytokines (tumor necrosis factor alpha, interleukin-6, interleukin 8, and interleukin-10), C-reactive protein, and procalcitonins in patients with community acquired pneumonia (CA) are associated with treatment failure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a simple and useful tool to identify patients at high risk of treatment failure in CAP.
the identification of markers for early treatment failure in CAP.
the development of a new approach to the treatment of patients with CAP, based on a better understanding of the pathophysiology of the disease, which could be of value for clinical practice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the combination of IL6, CRP and PTC is the best predictor of treatment failure.
serum levels of CRP and IL6 on day 1, and PCT on both day 1 and 72 h, are useful markers of treatment failure in patients with severe CAP.
the combination of CRP and IL6 levels on day 1 could be used to predict any treatment failure and that CRP and PTC levels on day 3 would be useful for predicting late treatment failure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the measurement of IL-6, IL-8, PCT and C-reactive protein on day 1 of hospitalisation may be useful in the early identification of patients at risk of treatment failure.
a combination of CRP and IL6 levels on day 1 is the best predictor for treatment failure.

the measurement of cytokine levels on day 1 may help in the identification of patients who will have treatment failure, and that the measurement of PCT and/or CRP may help in the early detection of patients who will not respond to treatment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the measurement of IL6, CRP and PTC on days 1 or 3 may help identify patients who are at high risk of treatment failure.
the combination of IL6 and CRPR on day 1 can be used to identify patients at risk for late treatment failure.
the measurement of cytokines and PCT on admission and after 72 hours may be a useful tool to identify patients with CAP who are likely to have treatment failure.
